Boost V2 with Chris Wilson DynISF V2 formula (2300/ln·TDD²·0.02)
Boost V3 with DynISF V3 — uses 7-day TDD only (no short-term blend), no BG velocity dampening
Boost v4.4 — adds post-SMB risk gate + meal-likelihood model (observability) on top of v4.2 baseline
Boost v4.4.2 (G3) — adds T4 velocity fallback (delta > 8) for sustained climbs + fast-carb override eBG escape (eBG > target+100), on top of v4.4.1 G3 release fixes

Boost V6 — Observe-Confirm-Commit dosing. Runs the Boost engine with V6\'s meal-aware SMB override. Select this as your APS to use V6; select plain \"Boost\" to run the base engine with the override in shadow.

When a rise is sharp AND accelerating AND the meal score corroborates (and you\'re awake, not exercising), V6 confirms the meal in one cycle instead of waiting — so fast carbs get covered ~15 min earlier. Replay-validated to avoid firing on sleep/compression. Toggle off to revert to the standard observe-confirm timing.

Confirms a meal one cycle sooner still when its signal is confirm-strength on two consecutive cycles — the same shot, delivered a touch earlier. Because it occasionally commits to a rise that would have faded, it adds a little insulin, so it is set automatically only for users whose recent low-glucose exposure is well within target. Default OFF; auto-config turns it on where it is safe. Leave off (or turn off) to keep the standard confirm timing.

Enforces a 25% floor on the composed soft-brake multiplier during active meal sessions above 160 mg/dL with eventualBG above target — fixes the soft-brake stack compounding to sub-pump-step zero doses mid-meal (July 2026). All hard gates and dose caps still apply. Default OFF. ENFORCED hypo-gate: the floor engages ONLY while BOTH your trailing 14-day time below 63 mg/dL (3.5 mmol/L) is under 2.0% AND your time below 70 mg/dL is under 3.5% — it is insulin-adding, so it stays suppressed (even when this is ON) if either low-exposure figure is higher, and auto-re-engages when both drop back under their limits.

When you are above 180 mg/dL but oref calculates no extra insulin is needed (it predicts you will come down on the insulin already on board), this delivers a small hold — up to 0.5 U, capped at your committed-cap and your IOB headroom — to bring highs down a little faster. It deliberately doses a touch more than the base algorithm on that high tail, so it is for users who prefer a firmer response to sustained highs. Excludes decelerating highs, sleep, and the post-rescue window; all hard hypo gates still apply. Default OFF. Uses the SAME ENFORCED hypo-gate as the brake floor: engages ONLY while your trailing 14-day time below 63 mg/dL is under 2.0% AND time below 70 mg/dL is under 3.5%, and auto-suspends if either rises.
Scales the catch-up dose at meal CONFIRMED. 1.0 = calibrated default; lower = gentler commit dose, higher = more aggressive. Range 0.7-1.3.
Multiplier on the ML hypo-risk damper floor. 1.0 = default; raise toward 2.0 for hypo unawareness or after a recent severe hypo. Range 1.0-2.0.
Scales the per-cycle insulin (aggression) budget. 1.0 = default; below 1.0 for sensitive users, above for resistant. Range 0.8–1.2.
Calculate ISF using Chris Wilson V2 formula: 2300/(ln(BG/insulinDivisor+1)·TDD²·0.02). TDD is required for V2 — falls back to profile ISF if data is incomplete
Percentage of algorithm-determined insulin to deliver as SMB. Default: 50
Maximum individual bolus from Boost. Default: 2.5 U
Maximum scale factor for percent-based Boost sizing between 108-180 mg/dL. Default: 200
Multiplier for calculated Boost insulin. Values >=3 disable Boost. Default: 1.0
Maximum IOB for accelerated bolusing. Above this, regular oref1 used. Default: 1.0 U

Total SMB insulin (U) that may be delivered in any rolling 60-minute window. Caps insulin stacking during sustained climbs. Set to 0 to disable. Factory default: 10 U (non-binding); auto-configuration tightens it to your own history (Confirmed cap + 2× Committed cap).

EXPERIMENTAL — when ON, the V6 observe-confirm-commit engine replaces the SMB dose on cycles SMBs are permitted. The base engine still controls basal and all safety gates. WARNING: this delivers insulin from an alpha algorithm; review closely and turn OFF to revert instantly.
Hard upper limit on V6\'s CONFIRMED commit-shot SMB. Lower this to tighten V6 during alpha. Default: 2.5 U
Hard upper limit on V6\'s per-cycle COMMITTED holding SMB. Default: 0.5 U

Fizzle-safe early primer delivered on an accelerating rise during OBSERVING — reclaims V1\'s ~15-min-earlier meal response. Additive up to this base; any velocity-scaled excess is netted off the CONFIRMED commit-shot (move, not add). 0 = OFF. Auto-config derives a per-user value.

Override: deliver the acceleration primer as a bolus even if auto-config routed you to the retractable temp-basal fallback (for hypo-prone users). Floors and the commit-shot net-off are unaffected. Default OFF (respect auto-config routing).

EXPERIMENTAL — learns your habitual meal times (from V6 meal commits) and applies a low target shortly before a learned meal so insulin is working when carbs land. Exercise and post-exercise recovery override it. When OFF it runs in SHADOW (logs \"V6 pre-meal WOULD apply\" without changing dosing) so you can verify the learned times first.
The low target applied during the pre-meal window. Lower = more pre-emptive insulin. Default: 72 mg/dL (4.0 mmol).
How many minutes before a learned meal the low target window OPENS. It closes 45 min before the meal. Default: 60 min.

Default value: 1.2\nThis is a multiplier cap for autosens (and deviation sensitivity) to set how high the sensitivity ratio can go, which determines how far ISF can be lowered during resistant periods.
Default value: 0.7\nThis is a floor for autosens (and deviation sensitivity) to set how low the sensitivity ratio can go, which determines how far ISF can be raised during sensitive periods.
Reference BG target for ISF calculation. Default: 99

Controls how much your current blood glucose level affects ISF. At 100%%, ISF is fully adjusted by BG (higher BG = stronger ISF). At 50%%, only half the BG-driven adjustment is applied. At 0%%, BG has no effect and ISF stays at the target-level value regardless of current BG. Default: 100
BG above this value is softened to reduce ISF aggressiveness at very high BG. Default: 210

This value is called max basal in OpenAPS context
This value is called Max IOB in OpenAPS context\nThis is maximal insulin in [U] APS can deliver at once.

Default value: 3.0 (AMA) or 8.0 (SMB). This is a setting for default carb absorption impact per 5 minutes. The default is an expected 3mg/dl/5min. This affects how fast COB are decayed, and how much carb absorption is assumed in calculating future predicted BG, when BG is falling more than expected, or not rising as much as expected.

Default value: 3 This is a key OpenAPS safety cap. What this does is limit your basals to be 3x (in this people) your biggest basal rate. You likely will not need to change this, but you should be aware that’s what is discussed about “3x max daily; 4x current” for safety caps.

Default value: 4 This is the other half of the key OpenAPS safety caps, and the other half of “3x max daily; 4x current” of the safety caps. This means your basal, regardless of max basal set on your pump, cannot be any higher than this number times the current level of your basal. This is to prevent people from getting into dangerous territory by setting excessively high max basals before understanding how the algorithm works. Again, the default is 4x; most people will never need to adjust this and are instead more likely to need to adjust other settings if they feel like they are “running into” this safety cap.

Default value: 2\nBolus snooze is enacted after you do a meal bolus, so the loop won’t counteract with low temps when you’ve just eaten. The example here and default is 2; so a 3 hour DIA means that bolus snooze will be gradually phased out over 1.5 hours (3DIA/2).

Default value: 0.5 This is another key OpenAPS safety cap, and specifies what share of the total insulin required can be delivered as SMB. This is to prevent people from getting into dangerous territory by setting SMB requests from the caregivers phone at the same time. Increase this experimental value slowly and with caution.
Default value: 0.5 This is the lower end of a linearly increasing ratio rather than the fix value above.
Default value: 0.5 This is the upper end of a linearly increasing ratio rather than the fix value above.

Default value: 0. The linearly increasing SMB delivery ratio is mapped to the glucose range [target_bg, target_bg+bg_range].\nAt target_bg the SMB ratio is smb_delivery_ratio_min, at target_bg+bg_range it is smb_delivery_ratio_max\nWith 0 the linearly increasing SMB ratio is disabled and the fixed smb_delivery_ratio is used.
Default value: 1 This is another key OpenAPS safety cap, and specifies by what factor you can exceed the regular 120 maxSMB/maxUAM minutes. Increase this experimental value slowly and with caution.

PKPD is enabled and OREF flags an imbalance. With your clinician, review DIA, peak time, and SMB damping together—not in isolation—using the advisor cards above as a checklist.
AutoDrive is on. Current MPC insulin-per-kg step is %1$s (preference). If highs persist without lows, discuss a cautious increase with your team; do not escalate repeatedly without review.
AutoDrive: lean toward less aggressive MPC
Frequent lows while AutoDrive is on (MPC step %1$s). Discuss reducing MPC aggressiveness with your clinician before any further increases.
Relief minimum factor is %1$s with elevated time below 70. Consider stepping toward ~%2$s with supervision, then reassess—tuning goes both ways.
Lower Red Carpet restore threshold (hypo context)
Restore threshold is %1$s while lows are frequent. A modest decrease toward ~%2$s may reduce late SMB snap-back—confirm with your team.
Priority MaxIOB factor is %1$s with significant hypo exposure. Consider ~%2$s under supervision rather than further increases.
Priority MaxIOB extra is %1$sU while lows are elevated. A step toward ~%2$sU may be safer than pushing headroom higher.
Profile ISF too aggressive vs TDD

Profile ISF %1$.0f mg/dL/U is %2$s%% lower than the 1700/TDD rule (~%3$.0f mg/dL/U for TDD %4$.0f U/day). This may cause overcorrection and hypos. Ask your clinician about raising ISF (gentler corrections).
Profile ISF too conservative vs TDD

Profile ISF %1$.0f mg/dL/U is %2$s%% higher than the 1700/TDD rule (~%3$.0f mg/dL/U for TDD %4$.0f U/day). This limits correction power and may prolong highs. Discuss a modestly lower ISF with your care team.

Basal is %1$s%% of TDD (%2$.1f U of %3$.0f U/day) — below the 40–50%% target. Low basal forces AIMI to rely heavily on SMBs for coverage, increasing stacking risk. Review basal segments with your clinician.
Basal is %1$s%% of TDD (%2$.1f U of %3$.0f U/day) — above the 40–50%% target. High baseline basal increases nocturnal hypo risk. Review overnight and daytime segments with your team.
PKPD is disabled when the TIR is low. Enabling is recommended for dynamic learning.
Persistent hyperglycemia: Reduce the daily insulin dose (from %1$s to %2$sh) to speed up the effect.
Postprandial hyperglycemia: Advance the peak (%1$s min) for greater responsiveness.
Resistance detected: Increase the ISF fusion (Max x2.0) for stronger corrections.
Detected hypoglycemia: Increase the DIA (%1$s → %2$sh) to reduce stacking.
Early hypoglycemia: Delay the peak (by 1–2 minutes) to smooth out the curve.
Risk of hypoglycemia: Increase damping to reduce SMBs at the end of the DIA.
Frequent lows with high ISF-fusion headroom: consider lowering max fusion from %1$sx to ~%2$sx with your clinician to cap aggressive corrections.
Persistent highs with strong SMB tail damping (floor %1$s): if hypos are rare, consider weakening the damping by raising the tail floor to ~%2$s to allow more late delivery.

Describe your current situation to help AIMI adapt insulin delivery
No AIMI understanding yet. It updates on each loop tick and when body signals or user context change.
No active contexts.\n\nUse quick presets or describe your situation.

Adjusts insulin using Health Connect vitals and a 28-pattern physiological catalogue (dawn, meals, stress, recovery). Does not enable or disable the physiological tree or Harmonia — those always run. Active patterns export to AIMI_Decisions.jsonl and feed RBT leaves and HTR caps.
28 hysteresis-gated patterns (sleep, HRV, meals, stress, cycle). Tap for details.

When the assistant is enabled, each loop tick runs the pattern detector on physio + CGM context. Matches export as physiological_patterns in AIMI_Decisions.jsonl and can cap HTR or inform RBT belief leaves. Requires Health Connect permissions for sleep and HRV when those sources are enabled. See repo docs/AIMI_PHYSIOLOGICAL_PATTERN_CATALOG.md for the full list.

Personal access token from cloud.ouraring.com — enables measured skin temperature deviation when Oura does not export it to Health Connect. Garmin users rely on inferred recovery rhythm from HC sleep/RHR.
See how AIMI interprets your current settings before simplifying them into behavior families.
View runtime, progress, and live status of all AIMI learning algorithms

Monitors hypo/hyper rates to decide whether to keep, hold conservative, or allow gentle basal/aggressiveness increases. Uses noise-weighted sample window (288 samples = 24h) with confidence scoring. Starts in WARMUP state until 36 samples (~3h) collected.

ML-powered ISF reactivity factor (0.5–1.5×). Combines 24h global analysis (60% weight) with 2h short-term analysis (40% weight). Reacts to TIR, CV%, hypo count, and oscillations. Short-term analysis available after ~30 min of CGM data.

3-tier basal adaptation: Short-term (30 min, 2h window, reacts to acute changes), Medium-term (6h, 24h window, intra-day patterns), Long-term (24h, fasting-based, structural TDD adjustments). Uses exponential weighting with configurable half-lives.

Learns personalized insulin DIA and peak timing via online gradient descent on post-bolus CGM data. Only learns on qualifying events (IOB > 0.3 U, BG > 75, no exercise, COB < 15 g, delta between -3 and +5). Uses anchor regularization to prevent drift. Needs multiple qualifying bolus events over days.
Learning only on qualifying post-bolus events (IOB > 0.3 U, no exercise, moderate delta). Check PKPD settings for current learned DIA and peak values.

Continuous 5-min gradient descent on sensitivity factor for Autodrive V3. Records 30-min-ahead BG predictions, then compares actual vs. predicted to adjust learnedSensitivityFactor (0.5–1.5). Very slow learning rate (0.005) for safety. First feedback at ~30 min.
Continuously running at each 5-min tick. Converges over hours-to-days. Check Autodrive control center for current sensitivity factor.

Detects nocturnal growth hormone-induced insulin resistance in pediatric patients. Uses existing loop signals (autosens, DIA, CGM noise) to derive NGR parameters — no independent warmup period. Readiness depends on autosens and ISF stability (typically hours).
Derives from autosens ratio and existing loop signals. Ready as soon as autosens has stabilized (typically within hours of loop start).

Learns per-phase basal and SMB multipliers across menstrual cycle phases (follicular, ovulatory, luteal). Uses EMA learning (alpha=0.10) per phase observation, clamped 0.70–1.30×. Persisted to disk. Needs 2–3 full cycles to converge.
Learns per-cycle-phase multipliers from CGM patterns. Needs multiple cycle observations. Current values visible in WCycle preferences.

Peak Governor learns insulin peak timing from observed CGM response to boluses. DIA Governor monitors observed vs. expected insulin duration. Both blend learned values with prior estimates using configurable learnedWeight. Learn from post-bolus events with strict quality gates.
Learn from qualifying post-bolus events alongside the PKPD estimator. Bias toward anchor values during early learning. Check PKPD advanced settings for current governor state.

Add a physio guard before going fully assertive on meals

Very assertive meal capture without any physio influence increases the risk of false meal interpretation during cortisol, dawn, or stress-driven rises. A moderate physio layer is a safer product baseline.
Raise autonomy to match this meal strategy

Your meal capture draft is already assertive, but AIMI autonomy is still too low to express it consistently. Move autonomy to assisted application so meal logic can act with clearer runtime authority.
Raise meal capture to match current autonomy

Your autonomy draft gives AIMI enough authority to act, but meal capture remains too prudent for that operating mode. Raising meal capture keeps the product behavior more consistent and easier to understand.
Reduce physio influence until sources are available
A strong physio setting without any active source or Oura connector creates an expectation gap. Moderate physio influence is a cleaner default until the body signals are truly observable.
